messages:
Marta L: Heads-up — traces + metrics are blowing up because of high-cardinality attrs (feature_flag, model_variant, region). Thinking we need an 'attr_density' heuristic to decide what to persist raw vs compact. Idea: compute per-tenant, per-attr density over a 24h window and if density < 0.001 we store a compacted representation (top-K values + hashed exemplar + bucketed fallback). Raw kept for dense attrs and short retention for raw vs long for compacted. Thoughts?

Kevin R: +1 on heuristic. Two quick concerns: (1) billing joins need stable keys — we should avoid hashing away billing-relevant attrs unless we keep a reconciliation path, (2) dashboards that do sudden group-bys will be surprised. We probably want an opt-out flag per attr for audit/billing.

Alex W: I like simple metric first: `density = unique_count / event_count`. threshold ~0.001 seems reasonable as a starting point. Also: top_k=50 per attr per tenant, then `other` bucket. Example pseudo: `if density < thr: persist(top_k, hashed_exemplar, bucket_scheme)` else `persist(raw)`. We should record the chosen policy in the envelope so queries can know how to interpret historical rows.

Samir: Query semantics caveat: compaction changes cardinality — we need regression alerts for prometheus/slo dashboards and a way to replay raw for short windows for debug. Suggest sticky sampling for a small % of events so we can reconstruct distribution with confidence. Also make compaction reversible for 7d (keep raw ephemeral archive).

Marta L: Good call on envelope flags — I was thinking gateway/enrichment layer to compute density and tag attr as `sparse:true` plus `compaction_policy:v1`. Ownership question: should this live in obs-gateway or in the ingest preprocessor?

Kevin R: Implementation note: do in gateway so tenants that send directly to our ingest (private) can still opt-in. But do not block on gateway-only; design the enrichment contract so any pre-ingest can set the policy header.

Alex W: I'll draft a tiny RFC with the scoring formula, example envelope fields and a ClickHouse schema diff. Quick DB example to show compact columns: ```sql
ALTER TABLE traces
ADD COLUMN attr_compacted_low_density Array(String) DEFAULT [],
ADD COLUMN attr_compacted_other Map(String, UInt64) DEFAULT {};
``` This lets us keep raw attrs for dense ones and shove compacted blobs for sparse ones.

obs-bot: FYI — created ticket INF-4231: "attr-density compaction prototype" and linked to backlog. https://redwood.example/t/INF-4231

Kevin R: Let's run a 2-week pilot with 2 tenants (one heavy, one typical). Add telemetry: density histograms, compaction false-positive rate, query-error counts. Also add an early-warning alert for >5% query regressions.

Marta L: Sounds good. Alex — can you drop the RFC draft in #eng-platform by EOD Thursday? I'll assign owners and pin pilot acceptance criteria. :thumbsup:
